thread:
elena: RFC follow-up — we need a concrete proposal for hysteresis-driven fallback + signal denoising for canary/A-B rollouts. Goal: stop flappy auto-fallbacks from transient noise, keep operator trust, and make breakglass simple.

raj: +1. My two cents: require a conjunction of signals (errors AND latency) over a sliding window, plus a confidence score from our eval anchors. Single-metric triggers lead to false positives.

maya: agree. We should weight signals by provenance: production user errors < synthetic eval regressions < golden prompt failures. The eval anchor should sample 1% of traffic with deterministic prompts.

sam: also watch cross-region skew. A global threshold will fire on regional blips. Proposal: per-region and per-tenant baselines, with a global aggregator that only triggers if majority of regions breach.

toni: runtime contract: auto-fallback must be an action the router can perform atomically: swap traffic to fallback variant, annotate requests with "fallback_reason" and a short provenance id. Provide an idempotent API so operator UI can re-run safely.

deploy-bot: [auto] rollout-monitor: canary v3 -> stable; monitoring enabled; sampled-eval job scheduled. :robot_face:

liz: session affinity and KV cache warmup matter — when we flip traffic some users will hit cold KV and look worse. Need a "grace window" where we allow a small % mirrored traffic to the fallback to warm caches. Also include prefix-affinity to reduce cache churn.

raj: rough pseudocode for detection: 
```
window = 5m
if error_rate(window) > 2% and p95_latency(window) > 500ms and eval_anchor_regressions > 0.5%:
  increment(fail_counter)
else:
  decay(fail_counter)
if fail_counter >= 3:
  trigger_fallback(reason="latency+errors+eval", cool_down=15m)
```

maya: store signal provenance with each trigger: metric names, sample sizes, anchor version, region list. That helps postmortem and avoids manual guessing. Also hash the prompt set version used for eval.

elena: good. For operator UX we should surface: top contributing signals, regions affected, and a single-click rollback/reinstate. Also indicate whether fallback was auto or manual.

sam: one more ops constraint: per-customer toggle to opt-out of auto-fallback. Some enterprise customers require manual approval. Default to enabled for self-serve.

toni: clarify terms in RFC: "rollback" = revert code/model config change; "fallback" = runtime routing to another variant. Fallbacks should be fast but reversible; rollbacks may require change control. Keep APIs distinct.

liz: add a circuit-breaker counter with exponential backoff so we don’t oscillate: each auto-fallback increases cool_down, manual override resets counters. Also expose metrics: fallback_count, avg_restore_time.

elena: action items: 1) raj + maya draft the detection algo with thresholds & decay math, 2) toni + liz propose router API and cache-warmup strategy, 3) sam to list per-tenant opt-out UX flow, 4) I'll write RFC outline. Can we aim for RFC draft by EOD next Wed?

raj: fine, will include tests for regional skew and synthetic perturbations.

maya: I'll wire sample anchor job and include example queries.

toni: will sketch a simple REST contract: /fallbacks/trigger and /fallbacks/status with idempotency token.

liz: will prototype mirror-warmup with slot-based ramp (0.5% -> 2% over 3m).

elena: thanks all — will assemble these into the RFC. If anyone has objections to the proposed conjunction approach, raise now. Otherwise I'll start the draft. :+1:
